title: Sustainable growth: why "successful" companies like Color, Groupon and Zynga fail
summary: Jason Cohen argues that investors and press reward growth and "shareholder value" while ignoring sustainability, producing companies that look successful and then collapse. He contrasts Groupon, Zynga and serial-exit founders with HubSpot, Rackspace, Freshbooks and SEOMoz, and says growth is necessary but not sufficient.

principles.text: Growth is necessary but not sufficient; if you want a lasting company, be honest about what "lasting" means.
principles.quote: But if your goal is to build a lasting company, be honest about what "lasting" means. **Growth is necessary, but not sufficient.**

principles.text: Growth bought with capital is not the same as building a product; force-fed revenue growth without long-term payback is not a business.
principles.quote: executives and investors are over-eager to value growth over sustainability (i.e. Groupon's engine that turned capital into revenue growth was a form of force-feeding rather than building a product)

principles.text: Validate the real value of your product to customers early; simple customer development reveals when claimed value is overstated.
principles.quote: the actual value of the product to small businesses wasn't as high as claimed, even though the simplest of customer development reveals this fact (ask any restaurateur)

principles.text: Real revenue and a big market are not enough if individual product wins are fleeting and you can't keep innovating enough to justify your size.
principles.quote: whose individual product successes are fleeting, who were financially successful at a certain scale, but it's doubtful they can continue innovating enough games to justify their current size

principles.text: Sustainable high growth comes from obsessing over customer service, retention and measurement, which also earns premium prices.
principles.quote: Rackspace whose maniacal obsession with excellence in customer service allows them to charge premium prices and sustain an amazing 30% annual growth even at the massive scale of $1b in revenue

principles.text: Sustainability isn't determined by how you finance the company; it's determined by what you decide to build.
principles.quote: Note that some of those companies were bootstrapped, some bootstrapped and took money later, and some had huge funding from the start. It's not about the financing path, it's about what you've decided to build.
